intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that autosomal recessive intellectual developmental disorder-37 (MRT37) is caused by homozygous mutation in the ANK3 gene, which encodes ankyrin G.

checks.claim: Autosomal recessive intellectual developmental disorder-37 (MRT37) is caused by homozygous mutation in the ANK3 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: in a consanguineous family with moderate intellectual disability (ID), an ADHD-like phenotype and behavioral problems, we identified a homozygous truncating frameshift mutation in the longest isoform of the same gene
checks.explanation: The abstract reports a homozygous ANK3 mutation in a consanguineous family with ID. It doesn't say 'autosomal recessive' or use the name MRT37; recessive causation is only implied.

checks.claim: The ANK3 gene encodes ankyrin G.
checks.evidence_quote: AnkyrinG, encoded by the ANK3 gene, is involved in neuronal development and signaling.

paragraphs.text: Iqbal et al. (2013) reported a consanguineous family in which affected members had moderate intellectual disability, an attention deficit-hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)-like phenotype, and behavioral problems.

checks.evidence_quote: in a consanguineous family with moderate intellectual disability (ID), an ADHD-like phenotype and behavioral problems
checks.explanation: The paper reports a consanguineous family with ID. MRT37 is OMIM's name for the disorder.

checks.explanation: Autosomal recessive inheritance is implied by a homozygous mutation in a consanguineous family, but the abstract never describes the transmission pattern.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a consanguineous family with MRT37, Iqbal et al. (2013) identified a homozygous truncating frameshift mutation in the longest isoform of the ANK3 gene, which they stated represented the first reported familial mutation in ANK3. Memory defects in a Drosophila knockdown model supported the causality of ANK3 mutations and the role of the gene in cognitive function.

checks.explanation: The abstract reports memory defects in a Drosophila knockdown model but doesn't say which gene was knocked down (the ANK3 ortholog).

checks.claim: The memory defects in the Drosophila knockdown model supported the causality of ANK3 mutations and the role of ANK3 in cognitive function.
checks.evidence_quote: The causality of ANK3 mutations in the two families and the role of the gene in cognitive function were supported by memory defects in a Drosophila knockdown model.

paragraphs.text: Iqbal et al. (2013) also described a patient with borderline intelligence, severe ADHD, autism, and sleeping problems in whom all isoforms of the ANK3 gene were disrupted by a balanced translocation. In contrast, the homozygous frameshift mutation in the consanguineous family with moderate intellectual disability affected only the longest ANK3 isoform. The authors concluded that their findings supported the suggested association of ANK3 with various neuropsychiatric disorders.

agent.process_note: Both papers were available only as abstracts, and I read both in full. Iqbal et al. (2013) found a homozygous truncating frameshift mutation in ANK3 in a consanguineous family. The abstract does not give the nucleotide or protein change, so no allelic variant entry could be written. It also does not give the number of affected people, their ancestry or their ages. The Hu et al. (2019) abstract does not mention ANK3 or any specific gene or family, so I did not cite it. No HGNC reference data was supplied, so the intro leaves out the gene's MIM number and chromosome location.
